NoteRegexAccessor::findall¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

TokenBatch NoteRegexAccessor::findall(std::string_view pattern,
                                      std::int64_t flags = 0) const

Extract Every Regex Match From Each Cell¶

findall(pattern) finds all non-overlapping matches of pattern in each text cell and returns them as a TokenBatch. It is the extraction member of the regex family — reach for it when the goal is to pull out substrings (numbers, IDs, dates, hashtags, symbol fragments), not to test for a match (Note::contains for literals) or to cut the string apart (split).

pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression. Matching scans left to right and does not overlap: after a match, the search resumes at its end.

Capture groups¶

If pattern contains at least one capture group, each result is the text of group 1; otherwise each result is the whole match. So \d+ yields the digit run, while id=(\d+) yields just the digits after id=. Groups beyond the first are not returned — restructure the pattern so the piece you want is group 1.

flags¶

flags is a bitmask of match options; flags <= 0 (the default) is plain case-sensitive ECMAScript.

Bit (value)

Effect

1 << 0 (1)

case-insensitive matching

1 << 1 (2)

multiline — ^ and $ also match at line breaks

The TokenBatch result¶

The matches from all cells are concatenated into one rank-one Text Note (batch.tokens()). batch.offsets() is a rank-one Int64 Note of length numel + 1; it records the boundaries, so cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). A cell with no match contributes an empty range (offsets[r] == offsets[r + 1]), never a placeholder token. Both halves retain Note ownership and can outlive the TokenBatch handle. Call integers() only when host code needs to traverse the offsets directly.

Failure¶

An invalid pattern (unbalanced parenthesis, bad escape) throws pluss::Error before any cell is processed.

Example 1: Digit Runs¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"Order 17 ships 2026-08-02", "Ticket 204 at 18:30", "none"});
const auto batch = n.regex().findall(R"(\d+)");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[7], dim=1, numel=7, encoding=utf8)
["17", "2026", "08", "02", "204", "18", "30"]
offsets: [0, 4, 7, 7]

Cell 0 produced four matches (offsets[0..1] = [0, 4)), cell 1 produced three ([4, 7)), and cell 2 ("none") produced none ([7, 7) — empty).

Example 2: A Capture Group Selects Part Of The Match¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"k=1; v=2", "x=9"}).regex().findall(R"(\w+=(\d))");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["1", "2", "9"]
offsets: [0, 2, 3]

The match is k=1, but the returned token is group 1, 1.

Example 3: Case-Insensitive Matching¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"AbCdE fF"}).regex().findall(R"([a-z]+)", 1);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["AbCdE", "fF"]

With flags = 1, [a-z]+ also matches upper-case letters, so each word is one match.

Example 4: The Same Pattern Without Flags¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"AbCdE fF"}).regex().findall(R"([a-z]+)");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["b", "d", "f"]

Case-sensitive, so only the lower-case runs match.

Example 5: A Cell With No Match¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"abc", "123"}).regex().findall(R"(\d+)");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["123"]
offsets: [0, 0, 1]

Cell 0 contributes the empty range [0, 0); cell 1 contributes [0, 1).

Example 6: An Invalid Pattern Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::make_note({"x"}).regex().findall("(");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

regex().findall: The expression contained mismatched ( and ).

See Also¶

  • NoteRegexAccessor::split: cut each cell at the matches instead of collecting them.

  • Note::contains: a literal yes/no test, no regex engine.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::tokens / Note::split: structural tokenizers that also return a TokenBatch.
